actions.q: Are actively managed ETFs cheaper than actively managed mutual funds?

fact_basis.fact: Funds (mutual funds and ETFs) must provide a standardized fee table in the prospectus with shareholder fees and annual operating expenses; the bottom-line figure is the expense ratio.
Page: actively managed ETFs exist; ETFs avoid capital gains distributions via in-kind redemption; mutual funds distribute gains; bid-ask spread cost.
fact_basis.source: quoted from this page (FAQ index fund; tax efficiency section; bid-ask FAQ)

actions.task: New FAQ, 3-4 sentences, NO numeric fee claims: the ETF wrapper does not set the fee; an active ETF and an active mutual fund each charge their own expense ratio, so compare the prospectus fee tables; active ETFs keep the in-kind tax advantage but add a bid-ask spread; the same cost-first rule applies. Link /guides/what-is-a-good-expense-ratio/.

actions.q: Do mutual funds charge sales loads or 12b-1 fees that ETFs do not?

fact_basis.fact: A front-end load is paid at purchase and a back-end load at sale; both are shareholder fees disclosed in the prospectus fee table.
12b-1 fees pay for distribution and sometimes shareholder services, are paid from fund assets, and by law cannot exceed 1 percent of average net assets per year.
The prospectus fee table does not show brokerage commissions or intermediary fees.

actions.task: New FAQ after the redemption-fee FAQ, 3-4 sentences: some mutual fund share classes charge front-end/back-end sales loads and 12b-1 fees (capped at 1% of assets/yr by law); no-load index funds exist; ETFs have no sales load but you pay trading costs; check the prospectus fee table.
